3.      PUBLIC HEARINGS

       a) BYLAW NO. 1681
           "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 477, (2762 and 2768 Claude Rd), 2017".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1681 at 5:32 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

                                                                                                   May 15TH, 2017
                                                                                                     Page 2 of 18




The City Planner advised that Matthew McKay, DB Services of Victoria Inc., has applied on behalf of
Matthew and Margaret McKay and Danny Lahnsteiner to amend the zoning of the properties at 2762 and
2768 Claude Rd from the R1 (One-Family Residential) Zone to the MU2 (Mixed-Use Residential
Commercial) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the construction of an eleven (11) storey residential building
consisting of approximately 117 residential dwelling units.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

In support of these/this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:
         • $1,525 per dwelling unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund, which may be reduced
               to $381.25 per unit if the project is secured as rental housing;
         • $610 per dwelling unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund, which may be reduced
               to $152.50 per unit if the project is secured as rental housing;
         • A Section 219 covenant, prior to Bylaw adoption, which secures the following conditions:
                   o That the owner will pay for and construct all works to restrict left turn movements
                       southbound on Claude Road to Goldstream Avenue prior to issuance of Occupancy
                       Permit;
                   o That the owner will provide a traffic and public safety plan and construction parking
                       management plan, prior to any onsite works and/or clearing, to the satisfaction of
                       the Director of Engineering;
                   o That the owner shall construct frontage improvements, works and services to the
                       standards of Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 and to the
                       satisfaction of the Director of Engineering; and
                   o   That  the owner will register on title a Section 219 covenant for stormwater
                       maintenance prior to the request for Occupancy Permit as a condition of rezoning.

Council also requested that the applicant provide a road dedication plan prior to Public Hearing, however
the applicant requests that the City accept a statutory right-of-way over the frontage of the property,
rather than dedication, to accommodate sidewalk, boulevard and street trees.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1681 closed at 5:34 p.m.

        b) BYLAW NO. 1684
            "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 479, (Omnibus No. 45 — Care Facilities), 2017".


The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1684 at 5:34 p.m.

Mayor Young advised members of the audience that any person present who believes that his or her
interest is affected by the proposed bylaws shall be given an opportunity to be heard on the matters
contained in the proposed bylaw. Those who wish to speak concerning this proposed bylaw should give
their name, address and views concerning the proposed bylaw. Mayor Young advised that after everyone
has expressed their views, he shall state three times "Is there anyone else who wishes to be heard", and
if no further views are forthcoming, the Public Hearing shall be declared closed.

The City Planner advised that the City of Langford has applied to amend the text of the Zoning Bylaw 300
in regards to permit the inclusion of Community Care Facilities to the list of uses allowed in the M1 (Light
Industrial) Zone.

Bylaw 1684 will amend the text within the Zoning Bylaw so that 'Care Facilities' will be permitted in the
M1 (Light Industrial) Zone.

As a light industrial zone, industrial businesses that operate within the M1 zone do not produce noxious
odours, dust, smoke or noise that would negatively impact the surrounding non-industrial uses. The
majority of parcels currently zoned M1 in Langford are found along Dunford Avenue, and act as a
transitionary industrial space separating heavier industrial uses and residential zones.

As many care facilities require expansive areas in order to congregate and assist to their clients, industrial
space within the Ml, light industrial, zone would be appropriate for adult patrons to receive care.

The bylaw being proposed would restrict care to adults and would not permit patrons or those providing
care to reside on parcels within the M1 zone as part of the care facility.

As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.

This proposal is consistent with the Neighbourhood Official Community Plan designations.

Advertisements have been placed as required by Council policy.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

The Mayor called a third and final time for presentation, there being none, the Mayor officially declared
the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1684 closed at 5:35 p.m.

That Development Variance Permit No. DVP17-0010 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford
to Casey Moore to reduce the required off-street parking (for one lot of a proposed three lot
subdivision) from the required 2 parking spaces to 0 parking spaces at 2840 Sooke Lake Rd subject to the
following terms and conditions:

1.   Appendix

     The site shall be developed in accordance with the site plan attached (Appendix A).

2.   Variances

     The following regulations of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 are varied under Section 498 of the Local
     Government Act:

     a) That Section 4.01.01 of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied from two (2) spaces per dwelling unit to
        zero (0) spaces per dwelling unit for proposed lot 1, subject to the following condition:
        i. An easement being registered on proposed lot 2 that permits the additional two (2) parking
          space from lot 1 onto this lot

     b) That Section 6.21.06(a) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied from 6.0m to 3.0m for the rear lot line
        of proposed lots 2 and 3, subject to the applicant registering, prior to issuance of a Building Permit,
        a Sec. 219 covenant registered in priority over all other charges on title that includes the following:
        I. That the City's standard interface fire hazard requirements for homes within the Interface
             Fire Hazard Development Permit Area will be met, as a condition of building permit;
        II. That the applicant will construct a non-combustible fence of at least 1.2m in height along the
             rear property boundaries;
        III. That the applicant accepts personally all liability stemming from works undertaken in
             Goldstream Park to date and that this liability is not transferred to future property owners.

source_identity.raw_motion_text:
That Council:

      1.    Proceed with the amendment to the text of the RR4 zone for the properties on 1323 and 1319
            Ravensview Drive, subject to the following terms and conditions:

            a)    That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant, registered
                  in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                   i. That no construction of building or subdivision or alteration of land may occur on
                      those lands contained on the eastern border of the property, and identified as the
                      common property with 1319 and 1323 Ravensview Drive and as shown in Figure 2 as
                      Lot 3 until all works and services required by Bylaw 1000 have been completed, to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
                  ii. That new and existing houses are required to connect to sanitary sewers when they
                      become available to the site, and that all costs associated with connecting to sewers
                      are the responsibility of the owners;
                 iii. That secondary suites are not be permitted; and
                 iv. That there may only be one residential dwelling per lot.

      2. Direct staff to proceed with consideration of the following variances for the proposed 3 lot
          subdivision of 1319 and 1323 Ravensview Drive subject to the applicant applying for the
          necessary development variance permit:

            a) Section 6.1.1 of the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
               allow for the creation of three lots that are not serviced by the municipal sanitary sewer
               system;

            b) Section 8.15.5 of the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No.1000 be varied to
               allow for the creation of three lots that require a reduction in fire flow but that do not
               contain residential fire sprinklers;

            c) Section 8.1.5 of the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied to
               allow for the creation of three lots that do not comply with the requirements of the BC
               Building Code in regards to sufficient water pressure;


            d) That Section 2.1.1 of the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 be varied
               to allow the creation of three lots without the provision of frontage improvements.

That Council:

      1. Give first reading to Bylaw Nos. 1694 and 1703 as presented to amend the zoning designation
          of the properties located at 3690 and 3694 Happy Valley Road from RR2 (Rural Residential 2)
          zone to R54 (Rural Small Lot 4) zone, subject to the following terms and conditions:

            b) That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                contributions per lot, prior to subdivision approval:

                   i.   $3960 per new one family lot towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                  ii.   $3660 per townhouse unit towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund;
                 iii.   $660 per new one family lot towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;
                 iv.    $610 per townhouse unit towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund;

            c)   That the applicant, prior to Bylaw Adoption of either Bylaw Nos. 1694 and 1703, provides
                 a Traffic Study and registers a road dedication plan with respect to the Happy Valley Rd
                 frontage to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

            d) That the applicant provides, prior to Adoption of Bylaw No 1703, a Section 219 covenant,
               registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the following:

                   i. That the applicant will complete full frontage improvements to Subdivision and
                      Development Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 standards to the satisfaction of the Director
                      of Engineering prior to subdivision approval; and
                  ii. That the applicant will install a signalized intersection at Happy Valley Road to the
                      satisfaction of the Director of Engineering at the time recommended by the Traffic
                      Study.
                 iii. That the applicant will provide a storm water management plan, and complete any
                      required improvements or upgrades to infrastructure to the satisfaction of the
                      Director of Engineering, prior to subdivision approval;

                 iv. That the applicant must submit and receive approval of the FUS calculations for the
                     site prior to subdivision approval;
                  v. That the applicant will incur all costs relating to infrastructure upgrades, including off
                     site works, required to manage the subject property's drainage concern, as a
                     condition of rezoning of the lands.
